findings.observation: Source File cards and Dialog disclosure show full filenames and clear filename-only wording. Escape closes the dialog; removing a file restores composer focus. The horizontal strip preserves vertical reading space.
Manual scroll-away remained at scrollTop 37 while content height increased from 1325 to 1647 px. Failure/retry, repeated questions and the seeded reload boundary worked.

An actual Return to latest click during growth did not catch the latest content. In the completion revisit the bottom gap was 1145 px at 1.51 s, 2134 px when the response became non-running at 5.05 s, and 798 px after another 600 ms. A second click after completion reached zero gap.

The first broad stop check failed because body text changed after running stopped. A narrower follow-up showed final Markdown text stabilizing, no running control, and composer focus. Deferred visible rendering settled for roughly one second. The first failure is retained and is not treated as proof of an indefinitely continuing response.
The source retains smooth/default return behavior during repeated growth, unlike P09's explicit instant behavior. This is a possible contributor, not a proven causal diagnosis.
The horizontal card strip reveals a subset of files at once, and modal filename lines can break at awkward characters/extensions. The dialog intentionally removes surrounding reading context.
Other browsers, physical mobile input, assistive technology and real backend behavior were not evaluated.

findings.observation: The mature workspace, compact File-family attachment strip, six-line composer and explicit text-bearing Return to latest control remain coherent across the viewed light/dark and narrow/compact conditions. File source and the synthetic adapter matched the foundation.

Full filename dialog disclosure, Escape trigger return and remove-to-composer focus worked. Manual scrollTop stayed 0 while height grew 1277 to 1599 px; return-to-latest bottom gaps stayed 0 across approximately 1.5 seconds while streaming.
The forced partial response failure was clearly visible; keyboard retry completed the long fixed response and reload returned to the seeded in-memory state.

Keyboard Stop ended the stream and text stabilized, but activeElement was BODY at 100 ms and remained BODY around 1.1 and 1.6 seconds. A separate targeted run reproduced the loss and required 12 Tabs through other controls to reach the composer.
After the 12-Tab recovery, a keyboard follow-up could be sent. This is a substantial continuity defect, not a complete keyboard trap or evidence of indefinite post-stop generation.
The horizontally browsed attachment strip hides some files outside the current view, and modal filename disclosure temporarily obscures the reading context.
All editor/branch paths, arbitrary content extremes, physical touch behavior and assistive-technology behavior were not certified.

material_unresolved_items: Keyboard Stop focus restoration requires a separately retained authorized repair and verification before unqualified T2 acceptance.
